questions.questionText: Your team wants to deploy a web application to Google Cloud without managing underlying virtual machines. The application is written in Go and packaged as a Docker container. Which fully managed serverless compute platform is specifically designed to run containerized web applications?

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Run is a fully managed serverless compute platform that abstracts away infrastructure management and allows you to deploy and scale stateless HTTP containers automatically.

why other options are wrong.Compute Engine Managed Instance Groups: MIGs require you to configure and manage virtual machine operating systems and auto-scaling rules, which is not serverless.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Functions: Cloud Functions deploys source code snippets (functions) directly, not Docker containers containing full web applications.
why other options are wrong.Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Standard: GKE Standard requires you to manage the underlying node pools (VMs), which is not fully serverless.

questions.questionText: You need to automatically execute a lightweight Python script every time a user uploads a new image to a Cloud Storage bucket. Which serverless compute option is easiest to configure for this event-driven task?

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Functions is an event-driven serverless compute platform. It natively integrates with Cloud Storage events (like object finalization/creation) to automatically trigger lightweight scripts (functions) in response to bucket activity.

why other options are wrong.App Engine Standard: App Engine is designed for hosting web applications. While it can process events, it requires setting up webhooks and Pub/Sub manually, making it harder than Cloud Functions.
why other options are wrong.Compute Engine: Compute Engine is IaaS. You would need to manage a VM, install software, and write a daemon to listen to events, which is not serverless or easy.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Dataflow: Dataflow is for complex data processing pipelines (ETL), which is overkill for a simple script triggering on a file upload.

questions.questionText: You are evaluating App Engine for a new application. The application experiences sporadic traffic and sometimes receives zero requests for hours. To minimize costs, you want the application to automatically scale down to zero instances. Which App Engine environment must you choose?

explanation.general explanation: The App Engine Standard environment is truly serverless and can automatically scale down to zero instances when there is no traffic, eliminating compute costs during idle periods.

why other options are wrong.App Engine Flexible Environment: The App Engine Flexible environment runs Docker containers on Compute Engine VMs. It requires at least one instance to be running at all times and cannot scale to zero.
why other options are wrong.App Engine Container Environment: There is no 'Container Environment' in App Engine (Flexible uses containers, but is not named this).
why other options are wrong.App Engine Hybrid Environment: There is no 'Hybrid Environment' in App Engine.

questions.questionText: When configuring a Cloud Run service, you want a single container instance to process up to 80 user requests simultaneously to optimize resource utilization and reduce the number of cold starts. Which setting should you adjust?

explanation.general explanation: In Cloud Run, the 'concurrency' setting determines the maximum number of requests that can be processed simultaneously by a single container instance. The default is 80, and it can be configured up to 1000.

why other options are wrong.Maximum instances: This limits the total number of container instances that can be spun up to handle traffic, not how many requests a single container can handle.
why other options are wrong.Minimum instances: This configures how many instances are kept warm to prevent cold starts, not the request density per container.
why other options are wrong.CPU allocation limit: This sets the CPU power available to the container, not the number of concurrent HTTP requests it accepts.

questions.questionText: Which two configurations help prevent excessive and unexpected billing charges for an internet-facing Cloud Run service subject to sudden, massive traffic spikes? (Select two)
options: Setting a strict Maximum Instances (max-instances) limit.
Using only the App Engine Flexible environment.
correctAnswers: Setting a strict Maximum Instances (max-instances) limit.

explanation.general explanation: To control costs on auto-scaling serverless platforms, setting a 'Maximum instances' limit physically stops Cloud Run from scaling beyond a defined threshold. Configuring Budget Alerts ensures administrators are notified if spending exceeds a specific amount.

Setting concurrency to 1 means a new container must be spun up for every single concurrent request, which drastically increases cold starts and costs.
why other options are wrong.Using only the App Engine Flexible envir: App Engine Flexible is not Cloud Run, and it cannot scale to zero, making it generally more expensive for spiky workloads with idle times.

questions.questionText: Google Cloud offers two generations of Cloud Functions. Cloud Functions (2nd gen) is built on top of which other Google Cloud serverless compute platform to provide longer execution times and larger instances?

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Functions (2nd gen) is built on top of Cloud Run and Eventarc. When you deploy a 2nd gen function, Google Cloud packages your function into a container and deploys it as a Cloud Run service behind the scenes.

why other options are wrong.App Engine Flexible: Cloud Functions 2nd gen is not built on App Engine Flexible.
why other options are wrong.Google Kubernetes Engine: While Cloud Run can run on GKE (Cloud Run for Anthos), the managed 2nd Gen Functions service relies on the fully managed Cloud Run infrastructure.
why other options are wrong.Compute Engine: Cloud Functions abstracts away raw VMs entirely.

questions.questionText: Your Cloud Run service needs to communicate with an internal Cloud SQL database that only has a private IP address within your Virtual Private Cloud (VPC). What feature must you configure to enable this outbound connectivity from Cloud Run to the VPC?
options: Serverless VPC Access connector (or Direct VPC Egress)
correctAnswers: Serverless VPC Access connector (or Direct VPC Egress)

explanation.general explanation: By default, serverless environments (Cloud Run, Cloud Functions, App Engine) run outside your VPC and cannot reach internal IP addresses. To route traffic from these serverless environments into your VPC, you must configure a Serverless VPC Access connector or use Direct VPC Egress.

why other options are wrong.Cloud NAT Gateway: Cloud NAT provides outbound internet access for private VMs; it does not connect serverless apps into a VPC.
why other options are wrong.VPC Network Peering: VPC Peering connects two VPCs together. Serverless environments are not VPCs themselves.
why other options are wrong.Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP): IAP is for securing user access to web applications, not for routing backend serverless traffic to a VPC.

questions.questionText: You are deploying a new version of your App Engine application. Instead of moving all users to the new version immediately, you want to send 10% of user traffic to the new version to monitor for errors. Which App Engine feature provides this capability natively?

explanation.general explanation: App Engine natively supports Traffic Splitting. You can deploy multiple versions of a service simultaneously and configure App Engine to route specific percentages of HTTP traffic to different versions for A/B testing or canary deployments.

why other options are wrong.VPC Service Controls: VPC SC is a security feature to prevent data exfiltration, unrelated to application deployment routing.
why other options are wrong.Identity-Aware Proxy: IAP secures web application access based on identity, not traffic percentages.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Load Balancing backend weights: While Load Balancers can do this for Compute Engine, App Engine has this feature built-in natively without requiring an external Load Balancer configuration.

questions.questionText: When writing code for Cloud Functions, what is the primary constraint regarding the programming languages you can use?
options: You must use one of the specifically supported official runtimes (e.g., Node.js, Python, Go).
You can use any language as long as you provide a custom Dockerfile.
You must write the code in Google's proprietary Dart language.
correctAnswers: You must use one of the specifically supported official runtimes (e.g., Node.js, Python, Go).

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Functions relies on managed runtimes. You must write your function using one of the officially supported language runtimes (like Node.js, Python, Go, Java, .NET, Ruby, PHP). You cannot bring custom containers to traditional Cloud Functions.

why other options are wrong.You can use any language as long as you: This describes Cloud Run, not Cloud Functions.
While Node.js is popular, Cloud Functions supports many other languages like Python, Java, and Go.
why other options are wrong.You must write the code in Google's prop: Dart is not a requirement for Cloud Functions.

questions.questionText: Users complain that your Cloud Run application takes 5 to 10 seconds to load if it hasn't been accessed for an hour, but loads instantly afterward. What configuration change is the most straightforward way to prevent this 'cold start' latency?
options: Configure a 'Minimum instances' (min-instances) value of 1 or more.
Increase the memory limit of the container.
Change the HTTP listener port from 8080 to 443.
correctAnswers: Configure a 'Minimum instances' (min-instances) value of 1 or more.

explanation.general explanation: Cold starts occur when a serverless platform scales to zero and must provision a new instance for a new request. By setting 'Minimum instances' to 1 or more, Cloud Run keeps instances warm and ready to serve traffic instantly, eliminating cold starts at the cost of baseline compute billing.

More CPU might speed up the application slightly, but it does not prevent the container from scaling to zero and requiring a full spin-up cycle.
why other options are wrong.Increase the memory limit of the contain: Memory does not prevent containers from scaling to zero.
why other options are wrong.Change the HTTP listener port from 8080: The listening port has absolutely no effect on scaling behavior.

questions.questionText: In the Google App Engine resource hierarchy, an Application contains one or more independent microservices. What are the two structural layers immediately below a 'Service' in this hierarchy? (Select two)

explanation.general explanation: The App Engine hierarchy is strictly defined as: Application -> Service -> Version -> Instance. A Service contains multiple Versions (deployments of code), and each Version runs on one or more individual computing Instances.

why other options are wrong.Clusters: Clusters are a Kubernetes (GKE) concept, not part of the App Engine resource hierarchy.
why other options are wrong.Nodes: Nodes are underlying VMs in Kubernetes or Compute Engine, not the logical terminology used in App Engine.

questions.questionText: To successfully deploy and run a custom Docker container on Cloud Run, the web server inside the container must listen for incoming HTTP requests. Which port must the container listen on by default?
options: The port defined by the $PORT environment variable (default 8080).
correctAnswers: The port defined by the $PORT environment variable (default 8080).

explanation.general explanation: The container contract for Cloud Run states that the container must listen for requests on the port defined by the `$PORT` environment variable provided by the Cloud Run environment. By default, Cloud Run sets this variable to 8080.

why other options are wrong.Port 443 (HTTPS): Cloud Run handles SSL termination at the edge. The internal container traffic is HTTP.
why other options are wrong.Port 80 (HTTP): While you could configure the service to pass 80, the strict requirement is to listen to the dynamic `$PORT` variable.
why other options are wrong.Port 22 (SSH): Cloud Run containers do not support SSH access via port 22.

questions.questionText: You have a batch processing script that takes 30 minutes to run and does not need to respond to HTTP requests. You want to run this script in a serverless containerized environment. Which Cloud Run feature should you use?

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Run Jobs is explicitly designed for running containerized scripts that run to completion (batch processing, database migrations) rather than continuously listening for HTTP web requests. It supports execution times up to 24 hours.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Run Services: Services are designed to listen continuously for web requests (HTTP), not for fire-and-forget background scripts.
why other options are wrong.App Engine Standard: App Engine Standard has strict request timeouts (60 seconds to 10 minutes) and is meant for web apps.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Functions (1st gen): 1st Gen Cloud Functions have a maximum execution timeout of 9 minutes, which is insufficient for a 30-minute script.

questions.questionText: Which two Google Cloud services are considered the primary fully managed, "serverless" compute platforms that abstract away underlying infrastructure provisioning and patching? (Select two)

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Run and Cloud Functions (along with App Engine Standard) form Google Cloud's core serverless compute stack. They automatically scale, require no infrastructure management, and charge only for what is used.

why other options are wrong.Compute Engine: Compute Engine is Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS). You manage the VMs, OS, and patching.
why other options are wrong.Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Standard: GKE Standard requires the user to manage the underlying Compute Engine node pools.

questions.questionText: Your Cloud Run service needs to securely read files from a specific Cloud Storage bucket. Following the principle of least privilege, how should you grant the Cloud Run service access to the bucket?
options: Assign a user-managed Service Account to the Cloud Run service and grant the IAM role to that Service Account.
Store a Service Account JSON key inside the Docker container image.
Make the Cloud Storage bucket publicly readable.
Grant the permissions to the default Compute Engine service account.
correctAnswers: Assign a user-managed Service Account to the Cloud Run service and grant the IAM role to that Service Account.

explanation.general explanation: The security best practice in Google Cloud is to create a dedicated, user-managed Service Account with the minimum required permissions (least privilege) and attach it to the Cloud Run service identity during deployment.

why other options are wrong.Store a Service Account JSON key inside: Storing hardcoded credentials inside an image is a severe security vulnerability.
why other options are wrong.Make the Cloud Storage bucket publicly r: This exposes the data to the entire internet, violating all security protocols.
why other options are wrong.Grant the permissions to the default Com: The default service account has broad Editor permissions on the project, which severely violates the principle of least privilege.

questions.questionText: You have deployed an App Engine application and need to schedule a specific URL endpoint (`/daily-report`) to be executed automatically every day at midnight. What configuration file must you create in your App Engine project to achieve this?

explanation.general explanation: In App Engine, scheduled tasks are defined using the `cron.yaml` file. This file specifies the URL to hit and the schedule (e.g., 'every 24 hours', 'every day 00:00') using a cron-like syntax.

why other options are wrong.app.yaml: The `app.yaml` file configures the runtime settings, scaling, and routing for the specific service, not scheduled jobs.
why other options are wrong.dispatch.yaml: The `dispatch.yaml` file routes incoming requests to specific App Engine services based on URLs.
why other options are wrong.index.yaml: The `index.yaml` file defines custom Datastore indexes.

questions.questionText: You are building a serverless architecture where a Cloud Function needs to process asynchronous events generated by other microservices. You want a highly reliable message queue to deliver these events to the function. Which service should trigger the Cloud Function?

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Pub/Sub is Google Cloud's asynchronous messaging service. Cloud Functions natively integrate with Pub/Sub; you can configure a function to be triggered automatically whenever a new message is published to a specific Pub/Sub topic.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Storage: Cloud Storage triggers functions based on file uploads/deletions, not general asynchronous microservice messages.
why other options are wrong.Cloud SQL: Cloud SQL is a database and does not natively push event triggers to Cloud Functions.
why other options are wrong.Compute Engine: Compute Engine is raw IaaS and does not act as a managed message broker.

questions.questionText: Using Eventarc, you can build event-driven serverless applications on Cloud Run. Which two Google Cloud services act as native event sources that can trigger Eventarc to route events to a Cloud Run service? (Select two)

explanation.general explanation: Eventarc allows you to route events from various Google Cloud sources to Cloud Run. Cloud Pub/Sub (messages) and Cloud Storage (object creation/deletion, often via Audit Logs) are primary native event providers.

why other options are wrong.VPC Peering: VPC Peering is a networking infrastructure feature; it does not generate application-level events.
why other options are wrong.Cloud NAT: Cloud NAT provides internet access for private VMs; it is not an event source.

questions.questionText: You have written a Node.js web application and created an `app.yaml` file in the root directory. Which gcloud CLI command is used to deploy this application to App Engine?

explanation.general explanation: The standard command to deploy code to App Engine using the configuration specified in the `app.yaml` file is `gcloud app deploy`.

why other options are wrong.gcloud run deploy: This command deploys container images or source code to Cloud Run, not App Engine.
why other options are wrong.gcloud functions deploy: This command deploys source code to Cloud Functions.
why other options are wrong.gcloud compute instances create: This command provisions raw virtual machines in Compute Engine.

questions.questionText: When designing an application for Cloud Run, what is a fundamental architectural requirement regarding how the container handles application data?
options: The container must be completely stateless.
The container must write all database files to its local disk.
The container must run a background daemon for persistent storage.
The container must share a file system with other running instances.
correctAnswers: The container must be completely stateless.

explanation.general explanation: The container contract for Cloud Run mandates that containers must be stateless. Since instances are spun up and destroyed dynamically, any state or data needed across requests must be stored in external managed services (like Cloud SQL, Memorystore, or Cloud Storage).

why other options are wrong.The container must write all database fi: Local disk is an ephemeral, in-memory file system. Data written there is lost when the container instance spins down.
why other options are wrong.The container must run a background daem: Background processes can be terminated at any time when the request finishes, preventing persistent background daemon storage.
why other options are wrong.The container must share a file system w: Cloud Run instances are isolated. While you can mount Cloud Storage via FUSE, the containers themselves do not inherently share a local file system.

questions.questionText: Which of the following scenarios is the MOST ideal use case for deploying a Cloud Function?
options: A lightweight, single-purpose snippet of code that acts as a webhook receiver.
A monolithic, legacy Java Enterprise application migrated from an on-premises server.
A high-performance relational database that requires sub-millisecond local disk latency.
A continuous video encoding pipeline that runs 24 hours a day without stopping.
correctAnswers: A lightweight, single-purpose snippet of code that acts as a webhook receiver.

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Functions are designed for simple, single-purpose, event-driven tasks—often called 'glue code'. Processing an incoming webhook is a perfect use case as the function spins up, processes the event, and spins down instantly.

why other options are wrong.A monolithic, legacy Java Enterprise app: Cloud Functions are for microservices/snippets, not large monoliths. App Engine or Compute Engine would be better.
why other options are wrong.A high-performance relational database t: Cloud SQL or Compute Engine is for databases. Cloud Functions are stateless compute.
why other options are wrong.A continuous video encoding pipeline tha: Cloud Functions have execution timeouts (up to 60 minutes for Gen 2). They are not meant for continuous 24/7 execution.

questions.questionText: You are deploying a public-facing website using Cloud Run. Which two Identity and Access Management (IAM) configurations are strictly required to allow any internet user to access the web application without needing a Google account? (Select two)
options: Assign the role to the special principal 'allUsers'.
Assign the role to the special principal 'allAuthenticatedUsers'.
correctAnswers: Assign the role to the special principal 'allUsers'.

explanation.general explanation: To make a Cloud Run service publicly accessible (unauthenticated), you must grant the 'Cloud Run Invoker' role (`roles/run.invoker`) to the special identifier `allUsers`. This explicitly allows anyone on the internet to send HTTP requests to the service.

why other options are wrong.Assign the role to the special principal: This would require the user to have a valid Google account to access the site, meaning it is not open to 'any internet user'.
The admin role grants permissions to modify and delete the service, which should never be given to public internet users.

questions.questionText: Every time you update the container image and deploy to an existing Cloud Run service, Cloud Run creates a new immutable snapshot of the code and configuration. What is this snapshot called?

explanation.general explanation: In Cloud Run terminology, a 'Revision' is an immutable, read-only snapshot of the code (container image) and the configuration (environment variables, limits) created every time you deploy an update. You can easily roll back to previous revisions.

why other options are wrong.Instance: An instance is a running execution of a container, not the configuration snapshot itself.
why other options are wrong.Cluster: A cluster refers to a group of nodes in Kubernetes, not a Cloud Run deployment snapshot.
why other options are wrong.Pod: A Pod is the smallest deployable unit in Kubernetes, not the configuration snapshot in Cloud Run.

questions.questionText: You are setting up a brand new App Engine application for your Google Cloud project. When you create your very first service, what specific name must this initial service be given?

explanation.general explanation: In Google App Engine, every application requires one central service. The very first service you deploy to App Engine must explicitly be named 'default'. Subsequent services can have custom names.

why other options are wrong.main: While common in programming, it is not the required App Engine service name.

questions.questionText: You are writing a 1st generation Cloud Function to process video uploads. Sometimes the processing takes a very long time. What is the absolute maximum execution time (timeout) limit you can configure for a 1st Gen Cloud Function?

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Functions (1st gen) have a hard maximum execution timeout limit of 9 minutes (540 seconds). If the script takes longer than this, it will be forcefully terminated.

why other options are wrong.60 minutes (3600 seconds): This is the maximum execution timeout for HTTP-triggered 2nd gen Cloud Functions.
why other options are wrong.1 minute (60 seconds): This is the default timeout for 1st gen, but it can be increased up to 9 minutes.
why other options are wrong.24 hours: This is the limit for Cloud Run Jobs, not Cloud Functions.

questions.questionText: By default, how does Cloud Run allocate CPU resources to your container instances regarding billing and processing?
options: CPU is allocated and billed only while the container is actively processing a request.
CPU is allocated and billed 24/7 as long as the revision exists.
CPU is allocated based on the size of the container image.
CPU is always allocated, but billing is paused during idle times.
correctAnswers: CPU is allocated and billed only while the container is actively processing a request.

explanation.general explanation: The default setting for Cloud Run is 'CPU allocated only during request processing'. The CPU is throttled to near zero when there are no incoming requests, and you are only billed for the exact milliseconds the container is actively handling a request.

why other options are wrong.CPU is allocated and billed 24/7 as long: This is how traditional VMs work. Cloud Run does offer an 'always allocated' setting, but it is not the default.
why other options are wrong.CPU is allocated based on the size of th: CPU limits are defined in configuration, not derived from image file size.
why other options are wrong.CPU is always allocated, but billing is: If CPU is always allocated (the alternate setting), you are billed for it even during idle times.

questions.questionText: Your organization requires that a Cloud Run service only communicates with an internal Cloud SQL database using private IP addresses. Which two networking configurations allow Cloud Run to send outbound traffic directly into your Virtual Private Cloud (VPC)? (Select two)

explanation.general explanation: To connect a serverless environment (like Cloud Run) to private resources inside a VPC, Google Cloud provides two primary methods: the older 'Serverless VPC Access connector' (which provisions bridge VMs) and the newer, faster 'Direct VPC egress' (which routes traffic directly without bridge VMs).

why other options are wrong.Cloud NAT: Cloud NAT is used to allow private VPC instances to access the internet outbound; it does not bridge serverless inbound to the VPC.
why other options are wrong.VPC Network Peering: VPC Peering connects two different VPC networks together. Cloud Run is a managed service outside your VPC, so you cannot natively 'peer' a VPC directly to Cloud Run.

questions.questionText: You are preparing an application to be deployed to the App Engine Standard environment. You need to configure the runtime (e.g., Python 3.9), the instance class, and scaling limits. Which file holds this configuration?

explanation.general explanation: The `app.yaml` file is the central configuration file for App Engine. It specifies the runtime, environment, instance scaling settings, environment variables, and request routing for your application.

why other options are wrong.Dockerfile: App Engine Standard relies on Google-provided runtimes. You do not provide a Dockerfile (that is used for Cloud Run or App Engine Custom Flex).
why other options are wrong.package.json: This file manages dependencies for Node.js applications, not the App Engine infrastructure configuration.
why other options are wrong.requirements.txt: This file manages Python library dependencies, not the App Engine infrastructure settings.

questions.questionText: Your development team is building a Cloud Function. Before deploying it to Google Cloud, they want to test the function locally on their own laptops to ensure it properly handles HTTP requests. Which Google-provided tool should they use?

explanation.general explanation: The Google Cloud Functions Framework is an open-source library that allows you to write lightweight functions and run them locally on your own machine. It wraps your function code in a local HTTP server for easy testing.

why other options are wrong.Cloud Build Local: This tool is used to execute Cloud Build pipelines locally, not specifically for running function code.
why other options are wrong.App Engine SDK: This is for testing App Engine applications locally, not Cloud Functions.
why other options are wrong.gcloud compute instances: This command provisions raw virtual machines in Google Cloud, unrelated to local developer testing.

questions.questionText: You have a batch of 1,000 video files stored in Cloud Storage that need to be processed. You want to execute a containerized script using Cloud Run Jobs to process them. How can you configure the job to process all 1,000 files in parallel simultaneously?
options: Execute the job as an Array task.
Deploy the container as a Cloud Run Service instead.
correctAnswers: Execute the job as an Array task.

explanation.general explanation: Cloud Run Jobs supports 'Array tasks' (or parallel execution). You can configure a single job execution to fan out into an array of independent tasks (e.g., 1,000 tasks) that run in parallel, each processing a different index or file.

why other options are wrong.Increase the concurrency setting to 1,00: Concurrency determines how many incoming HTTP requests a single Cloud Run Service container handles. It does not fan out background jobs.
why other options are wrong.Deploy the container as a Cloud Run Serv: Services are for listening to HTTP requests, not efficiently executing 1,000 isolated batch processing tasks simultaneously.
This keeps 1,000 instances warm for a service to handle HTTP traffic; it does not trigger a job to execute 1,000 scripts in parallel.
